critical_code_review_comments: geo_search.company_contains_term threshold len(norm_term) <= 2 is reasonable but documented only in code comments. Add a short README/docstring example: 'Beta' → substring (matches BetaSystems081, BetaTech065), 'sa' → whole-word (avoids matching every 'SAS' suffix), 'a' → whole-word (avoids matching everything).

SearchStudentsPage.jsx line 67 ternary `user?.role !== 'company' && user?.role !== 'admin'` works but a positive allowlist `!['company','admin'].includes(user?.role)` is more maintainable when more roles are added later (e.g. 'school' or 'recruiter').

Header.jsx lines 130-131 duplicate the same menu entry for company & admin with two different data-testids. Consider a single conditional `{(user.role==='company'||user.role==='admin') && <DropdownMenuItem … data-testid={user.role==='admin'?'menu-search-students-admin':'menu-search-students'}>` to avoid duplication.

Backend: routes/offers.py /api/offers?company=… now triggers substring search → make sure the same logic flows into /api/external-offers/all and /api/francetravail/search (confirmed via tests, all return 0 for 'Sofratom') — good consistency.

rca of the issue: Original RCA was correct and the fixes target it precisely: (1) Before iter21, company_contains_term required regex \b<term>\b which means 'Beta' would only match a token boundary — 'BetaSystems081' has no boundary between 'Beta' and 'Systems', so it was excluded. New behavior: for 3+ chars do plain `norm_term in norm_name`, keeping whole-word ONLY for ≤2 chars to avoid matching 'sa' against everything. Verified: 'Beta'→3 matches, 'Bright'→1 match, 'BetaSystems081'→2 matches, 'a'→0, 'Sofratom'→0 (internal+external+FT). (2) SearchStudentsPage previously rejected admin role on the client (server already accepted it) — line 67 now includes 'admin'. Header gained a parallel menu item with a distinct data-testid for discoverability. Verified end-to-end: admin login → /search/students → 'Lucas' → Lucas Martin card.
